bib.title: Meta-RL Induces Exploration in Language Agents

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "Meta-RL Induces Exploration in Language Agents" (method name LaMer), Yulun Jiang*, Liangze Jiang*, Damien Teney, Michael Moor, Maria Brbic (EPFL, ETH Zurich, Idiap). Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2026; arXiv:2512.16848v2, 8 Mar 2026 (v1 Dec 2025). First author: Jiang (equal with L. Jiang). Code: github.com/mlbio-epfl/LaMer.

COVERAGE: 25 of 25 pages, 78,670 chars, all read except the references (skimmed) and the long prompt listings in App. B (skimmed). App. E (one MineSweeper reflection example) was read only in part.

CLAIMS (ranked)
1. LaMer beats the best RL baseline (GiGPO) on pass@3 in all three main environments. The gap comes from attempts 2 and 3, not attempt 1.
 number: pass@3 Sokoban 55.9 vs 44.1; MineSweeper 74.4 vs 55.1; Webshop 89.1 vs 75.2. Pass@1 is 42.4 vs 41.6 on Sokoban, 44.1 vs 52.0 on MineSweeper and 67.8 vs 73.4 on Webshop.
 setup: Qwen3-4B, non-thinking mode, GiGPO optimizer, N=3 episodes per trial, group size 8. Metric is success within 1/2/3 attempts. Pass@k here means sequential attempts with reflection, not independent samples. The paper reports no seeds, variance or confidence intervals.
 quote: "LAMER achieves a 55.9% pass@3 success rate, substantially outperforming the 44.1% from the strongest RL baseline (GiGPO) and 12.9% from prompting-based methods." (p.7)
 Other rows (p.6, Table 1): GRPO 22.9/26.4/27.0 on Sokoban and 72.9/73.0/73.0 on Webshop; Reflexion (prompting) 6.4/9.8/12.1 on Sokoban.
2. The abstract's "11%, 14%, 19%" gains are pass@3 gains over RL, but the text and abstract do not match on which environment gets which number. The abstract says 11/14/19 on Sokoban/MineSweeper/Webshop. The p.7 text says MineSweeper +19 and Webshop +14. Table 1 gives 11.8 (Sokoban), 19.3 (MineSweeper) and 13.9 (Webshop), so the table matches the text and the abstract order is wrong.
 quote: "On the MineSweeper environment LAMER reaches 74.4% pass@3 success rate, which is 19% higher than the best RL-trained model. On the Webshop environment, LAMER also performs 14% better" (p.7)
3. Compute-matched comparison. RL uses group size 24 and Meta-RL uses N=3 episodes x group 8, so each gradient step sees the same number of trajectories. Meta-RL costs about 2x wall-clock because episodes in a trial must be sampled sequentially.
 quote: "we observe around twice the training time cost for LAMER in our current implementation." (p.9)
4. Exploration is preserved. Trajectory-distribution entropy is highest for the base model, drops under RL and stays higher under Meta-RL (Fig 1, Fig 3). The paper does not give numeric entropy values in the text.
 quote: "RL-trained agent reduces diversity and converges toward more deterministic behaviors. In contrast, LAMER trained with Meta-RL preserves a higher level of diversity than RL baselines" (p.7)
5. Ablation isolating the cross-episode part (App. D.2, Table 5, pass@3, p.24). Giving the GiGPO RL agents inter-episode memory at test time helps only a little and the gap to LaMer remains. This indicates the cross-episode training objective matters, not just reflection at test time.
 number: GiGPO w/o memory 44.1/55.1/75.2 vs w/ memory 47.9/60.4/74.0 (Sokoban/MineSweeper/Webshop). LaMer 55.9/74.4/89.1.
 quote: "LAMER still substantially outperforms RL baselines across all the environments" (p.24)
6. Memory-content ablation (Table 3, p.9, pass@3). Reflection-only memory is as good as or better than the default of history plus reflection.
 number: Trajectory-only 34.8 / 69.5 / 89.3; Reflection-only 56.4 / 80.5 / 92.8; Both (default) 55.9 / 74.4 / 89.1.
 quote: "the reflection-only configuration also outperforms the default setting in LAMER (which contains both trajectory and reflection) across all environments." (p.9)
 The authors' explanation, "more concise and focused guidance", is a hypothesis.
7. gamma_traj (cross-episode discount) ablation (Fig 5, p.9). Larger is not monotonically better. The default is 0.6; Sokoban and Webshop do best at intermediate values, MineSweeper at about 0.9. Values swept: 0.3, 0.45, 0.6, 0.75, 0.9. Results are shown only as plots.
 quote: "a larger value of γtraj does not necessarily lead to better final performance on pass@3, instead, the optimal setting of γtraj varies across different environments." (p.9)
8. Harder-task generalization (Fig 4, p.8). Trained on Sokoban 6x6 with 2 boxes and MineSweeper 6x6 with 3 mines, then tested with more boxes (2-5) or mines (3-6). Meta-RL is better at every level, with a 10-point gap on the hardest Sokoban and 5 points on MineSweeper. Read from plots, no table.
9. Out-of-distribution on ALFWorld (Table 2, p.8). Trained on Pick, Look, Clean, Heat and tested on the held-out Cool and Pick2. The table does not say whether the metric is pass@1 or pass@3.
 number: Cool RL 58.1 vs Meta-RL 81.0; Pick2 36.0 vs 50.2. In-distribution Meta-RL vs RL: Pick 97.7/95.5, Look 100.0/83.0, Clean 90.2/67.9, Heat 89.5/86.6.
10. Second model (App D.1, Table 4, p.24). Llama3.1-8B-Instruct, only GiGPO vs LaMer, on Sokoban and MineSweeper only.
 number: pass@3 Sokoban 20.3 vs 6.3; MineSweeper 65.6 vs 42.2. Pass@1 on MineSweeper is 47.7 vs 39.1.
11. Training details (App C, p.24): lr 1e-6, Adam; batch 16 / 300 epochs for Sokoban and MineSweeper; batch 8 / 150 epochs for Webshop and ALFWorld. Reward 10 for success and 0 otherwise. Temperature 1.0 in rollout and 0.7 at eval. Max 1024 output tokens. Built on verl and verl-agent.

METHOD (for the note)
- Each trial is N sequential episodes from the same initial state. The trial stops early on success. After each failed episode the agent writes a reflection (<remark> tags). That reflection is itself trained with the next episode's reward.
- Cross-episode return: G_t^(n) = g_t^(n) + sum_{m>n} gamma_traj^(m-n) g_0^(m) (Eq. 4). It is optimized with standard policy-gradient methods (GiGPO is the default; PPO and GRPO are said to be compatible).
- The adaptation is in context, with no gradient step at test time.

LIMITS
- The authors concede three limits. Rollouts are sequential, so training takes about 2x as long. A stronger reasoning model or better advantage estimation might help (a hypothesis, not tested). Transfer is only to harder or similar tasks, not to truly novel environments.
- Not shown: results on tasks with dense or non-binary reward; multiple seeds or variance; models above 8B; thinking-mode models; a plain-RL baseline given N sequential attempts at train time other than the test-time-memory variant in Table 5. Table 1 omits ALFWorld; it appears only in the OOD experiment.
- The RL baselines in Table 1 have no access to inter-episode memory (the authors say this follows prior work).
- Pass@1 is not improved on MineSweeper or Webshop. LaMer trades some first-attempt performance for later gains.
- Reflexion and ReAct are only prompting baselines on the untrained base model.

BUILDS ON: Duan et al. 2016 (RL^2); Wang et al. 2016; Finn et al. 2017 (MAML); Beck et al. 2025 (meta-RL tutorial); Shinn et al. 2023 (Reflexion); Feng et al. 2025 (GiGPO / verl-agent); Shao et al. 2024 (GRPO); Schulman et al. 2017 (PPO); Ahmadian et al. 2024 (RLOO); Laskin et al. 2023 (algorithm distillation); Snell et al. 2025 and Setlur et al. 2025 (test-time compute); Qu et al. 2025 (single-turn meta-RL); Krishnamurthy et al. 2024 (LLMs do not explore in context).

CODE: none in the paper.

FIGURES: Fig 1 (p.2) is the MineSweeper RL vs Meta-RL trade-off between trajectory diversity and success rate. Fig 2 (p.5) contrasts independent RL rollouts with sequential rollouts plus reflection, and is the best single picture of the method. Fig 3 (p.7) shows trajectory entropy for base, RL and Meta-RL. Fig 5 (p.9) shows the gamma_traj sweep.

QUOTES FOR THE NOTE
- "the agent internalizes a learning algorithm that explicitly incentivizes exploration for improved downstream exploitation." (p.2)
- "Ideally, small γtraj biases the objective towards early episodes and will lead to rapid exploitation to solve the problem. In comparison, a larger γtraj emphasizes long-horizon return and therefore encourages more exploration at the early stage." (p.5)
- "The key difference is that the RL rollouts are independent, whereas in Meta-RL each episode is conditioned on the preceding rollouts within the trial." (p.5)

PROBLEMS: There are no embedded instructions. Extraction is clean; figures are plots, so the Fig 4 and Fig 5 numbers cannot be read exactly. The abstract's per-environment ordering of 11/14/19 is inconsistent with Table 1 (see claim 2). The extracted text is saved at /tmp/jiang.txt.
